text:
maya: quick question — streaming telemetry bursts are creating big billing spikes for a handful of small tenants. thinking through tradeoffs: pre-aggregate/drop at the edge (ingest) vs global early-drop after enrichment. thoughts?

alex: agreed this popped up in the billing dashboard. pre-agg seems appealing for cost but we lose billing fidelity and later attribution.

riya: pre-agg = cheaper ingest + faster tail latency. downside: if we pre-aggregate incorrectly we break per-route chargeback. can we do per-tenant knobs?

oliver: per-tenant knobs add auth/scale complexity. maybe adaptive shedding based on tenant budget metadata? i.e., tenant has "cost_budget" in profile and we drop after budget exceeded.

maya: adaptive budget-aware shedding sounds neat, but we need an authoritative source for budgets that is low-latency and available at edge. don't want a sync call on every trace.

sam: what if edge keeps a local token-bucket cache for budgets + periodic refresh? cheaper than per-request lookup and allows burst smoothing.

riya: that helps but still unsure about enrichment: many of our billing keys come from late enrichment (customer labels added by enricher). if we drop early we might miss proper attribution and charge to the wrong bucket.

oliver: can we split the pipeline: do light-weight envelope-level pre-agg (count/stats) then keep a small sampled subset of full spans for late enrichment? basically two-tier: counters always, full traces sampled.

maya: two-tier seems promising. counters give cost signal and budget enforcement, sampled traces retain attribution and debugging. we need to ensure sampled set size suffices for regressions.

alex: agree. add config suggestion: edge emits aggregated envelope: {"tenant_id", "counter_delta", "approx_percentile_seq_len"} and a sample flag for full-forward. simple and cheap.

sam: here's a rough config snippet for the edge token-bucket + sampling policy:
```
edge.configs.telemetry_throttle = {
  bucket_capacity: 10000,
  refill_per_min: 50000,
  sampling_rate: { default: 0.01, high_traffic: 0.001 },
  sample_quota_per_bucket: 5
}
```

riya: a couple concerns: 1) billing reconciliation — aggregated counters must be eventually reconciled with full-enriched traces to avoid double-counting/under-counting, 2) query UX — customers expect per-request chargeback sometimes.

oliver: for reconciliation we can run a nightly join job: aggregate counters vs enriched samples extrapolated. We must quantify error bounds and surface them to billing UI.

maya: operational note: fallback when enrichment fails (e.g., enricher down) — we should have a safe default: mark aggregated envelopes as "unattributed" and route to a low-cost bucket instead of dropping silently.

alex: +1. also need circuit-breaker telemetry so SRE can see how much pre-agg/drop is happening and per-tenant drop rates. add metrics: preagg_dropped_count, preagg_sampled_rate_by_tenant.

observability-bot: new alert rule suggestion: alert if preagg_dropped_count_rate > 0.5% overall or any tenant > 2% for > 5m. link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/preagg-drop

sam: implementation notes — edge needs a small persistent state store (LSM or in-memory with periodic snapshot) for token buckets so restarts don't reset budgets entirely. lightweight and local is fine.

riya: question on privacy/compliance: sampled traces might contain PII that aggregated counters don't. sampling policy must obey tenant compliance flags (e.g., "no_payload_sampling").

maya: good catch. sampling should be gated by tenant-level policy. if "no_payload_sampling" true then we only emit counters and route to low-cost retention.

alex: final call: propose RFC follow-up with 3 concrete designs: A) naive global early-drop, B) per-tenant token-bucket + sampling (two-tier), C) enrichment-first w/late-drop + backpressure. include cost sims and error-bound estimates.

maya: I'll draft the follow-up RFC with sims and prioritization matrix. tagging @alex @riya for review. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
